title: Drug Sensitivity Assays of Human Cancer Organoid Cultures
author: Hayley E. Francies
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bpsgmnbw

steps.title: Design drug plate layout
steps.instruction: Plan the layout of the drug screening plate according to Note 4 and Fig. 2.

steps.title: Reconstitute drugs in DMSO
steps.instruction: Reconstitute each drug in 100 % DMSO, store frozen at –80 °C or in StoragePods® at room temperature (moisture‑free, low‑oxygen, UV‑protected) as per Note 5.

steps.title: Prepare master drug stocks
steps.instruction: Make master stocks at 1,000–10,000 × the desired maximum screening concentration.

steps.title: Create stock plate with robot
steps.instruction: Using a Biomek FX, cherry‑pick master stocks into a 384‑well polypropylene stock plate. If the master stock is 1,000 ×, transfer directly; if >1,000 ×, dilute in DMSO during transfer so every well ends up at 1,000 ×.

steps.title: Generate source plate with dilutions
steps.instruction: From the stock plate, generate a 384‑well low‑dead‑volume source plate containing the drugs and half‑log dilution series in DMSO; each well holds 10 µL at 1,000 × the final concentration. One source plate can serve multiple screening plates and dates (Notes 6, 7).

steps.title: Seal and store plates
steps.instruction: Seal stock and source plates with adhesive foil. Store in StoragePods® or at –80 °C, limiting freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Dispense BME‑2 layer
steps.instruction: Program the FluidX XRD‑384 to dispense 8 µL. Flush the dispenser sequentially with ethanol, sterile water, then organoid media. Prime with 7.5 mg/mL BME‑2 until tubing is filled. Keep BME‑2 chilled and dispense 8 µL of 7.5 mg/mL BME‑2 into every well of a 384‑well flat clear‑bottom polypropylene plate.

steps.title: Centrifuge and polymerize BME‑2
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the plate at 182 × g, °C, 1 min to spread BME‑2 across the well bottom. Then incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for ≥20 min to allow polymerization (Note 8).

steps.title: Prepare organoid suspension
steps.instruction: Culture organoids embedded in 10–15 µL droplets of 7.5 mg/mL BME‑2; seed 15 droplets per well of a 6‑well plate with 2 mL organoid media. Harvest by scraping droplets, mix with media using a 1 mL pipette (avoid single‑cell dissociation), transfer to a 15 mL tube and centrifuge at 364 × g, °C, 2 min. Aspirate supernatant and resuspend pellet in 5 mL drug‑screening media.

steps.title: Count organoids
steps.instruction: Place three 10 µL droplets of the suspension on a microscope slide, count organoids in each droplet, calculate the average, and multiply by 100 to obtain organoids · mL⁻¹ (Notes 9, 10).

steps.title: Adjust organoid concentration
steps.instruction: Dilute or concentrate the suspension to 15,000–20,000 organoids · mL⁻¹. For two 384‑well plates you need 35 mL at 15,000 organoids · mL⁻¹, which requires roughly three confluent 6‑well plates (≈525,000 organoids).

steps.title: Add media to column 1
steps.instruction: Ensure the XRD‑384 is primed, then dispense 32 µL drug‑screening media into all wells of column 1 (media‑only control).

steps.title: Dispense organoid suspension
steps.instruction: Program the XRD‑384 (flush as in step 7) to dispense 32 µL organoid suspension into every well except column 1, giving a total well volume of 40 µL.

steps.title: Settle organoids overnight
steps.instruction: Incubate the plates at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ overnight (until the following day) to allow organoids to settle (Note 12).

steps.title: Inspect organoid health
steps.instruction: Using a phase‑contrast microscope, manually inspect each plate for organoid health before drug addition.

steps.title: Acoustic dispensing of compounds
steps.instruction: With an Echo 555, dispense 40 nL of each compound (prepared at 1,000 ×) from the source plate into the assay plate to achieve a final 1 × concentration and 0.1 % DMSO.

steps.title: Incubate with drugs
steps.instruction: Return plates to 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ incubator and incubate up to 6 days; longer incubations risk evaporation and reduced data quality.

steps.title: Post‑treatment inspection
steps.instruction: After drug incubation, manually check under the microscope that positive‑control wells show organoid death and negative‑control wells remain healthy.

steps.title: Add CellTiter‑Glo 2.0
steps.instruction: For each 384‑well plate, prepare ~4 mL CellTiter‑Glo 2.0 (add 10 mL to the calculated volume to compensate for XRD‑384 dead volume). Remove plates from incubator and equilibrate to room temperature for 10 min. Program the XRD‑384 (flush as before, prime with CellTiter‑Glo 2.0) to dispense 10 µL into every well.

steps.title: Develop luminescent signal
steps.instruction: Incubate plates at room temperature for 20 min, then read luminescence on a Paradigm plate reader.

steps.title: Calculate quality metrics
steps.instruction: Compute coefficient of variation (CV) of negative controls (acceptable < 0.22), Z‑factor using positive and negative controls (acceptable ≥ 0.4), and DMSO effect ratio (negative‑control DMSO / without DMSO; acceptable 0.8–1.2).

steps.title: Normalize and analyze data
steps.instruction: Normalize each well: (Raw − Mean positive)/(Mean negative − Mean positive). Perform dose‑response curve fitting to obtain IC₅₀ and AUC values.
